_comment: #508. Mission Victorians carrying a Latino paint tradition: this is the most saturated palette
in the library and deliberately so - it is the district that should be visible from three blocks
away. Base runs cream and wheat next to ochre, terracotta, a teal-green and a dusty rose, and
the draw is even, so a block is genuinely mixed rather than cream with occasional colour.
Accent1 is where the contrast lives: cream, a deep teal and an oxblood, which is how Mission
trim actually behaves - a strong colour outlining a strong colour. Accent2 ramps gold into burnt
orange for sills, hoods and cornice bands.
Sign is authored here (unlike the residential palettes) because mission_storefront ships and the
district's shopfronts are half its character - see the note in the coverage test about Sign
being a texture role that nothing currently resolves through the palette.
Authored, not verified in an Editor.
